Full version: http://www.bmj.com/cgi/reprint/328/7454/1459 (accessed 09/11/07) Lichen Lichen planus (p.1580) is generally controlled with corti- costeroids applied topically or, occasionally, injected intra- lesionally; systemic corticosteroids (usually prednisone or prednisolone) are used for severe erosive lichen planus, generalised cutaneous disease, and acute exacerbations.1,2 Prednisone has generally been used in oral doses of 30 to 60 mg daily, for courses of 4 to 6 weeks.1 Shorter courses may be of value: prednisolone (30 mg daily for 10 days) was reported to be effective and safe for mild or moderate- ly severe lichen planus.3 The use of topically applied corticosteroids in the treat- ment of lichen sclerosus (p.1580) has been discussed.4,5 Relief from vulvar pruritus is obtained in most cases with a potent corticosteroid preparation, such as clobetasol pro- pionate, applied twice daily for up to 3 months before ta- pering the dose.4 1.
